text:
COP fell 0.66% to $145.55 today, a small pullback after jumping 3.8% on Friday (Oct 16). The timing suggests profit-taking following a strong two-week rally—the stock is up 13.4% since early October, driven largely by the surge in oil prices (US crude sits at $101.91/barrel, up sharply from the $85–$90 range earlier in the month) sparked by Houthi attacks on Saudi oil infrastructure and threats to regional supply announced over the weekend.

The modest loss today doesn't reverse the underlying tailwind. World oil prices remain elevated at $126.55/barrel, and geopolitical risk in the Middle East—with Iran-backed militant threats continuing and Saudi Arabia postponing its major investor conference—keeps supply uncertainty high. For a major oil producer like this company, that environment is generally positive, even if traders are taking profits on a very strong week.
